title: What is a Job?
content:
## What is a Job?

In Emergent, a **job** is a single application or project. Every time you describe a new app and start building, you create a job. The term "job" appears throughout the platform — in your workspace, the sidebar, notifications, and billing — and always refers to one discrete build.

A job encompasses everything related to that app: the chat history where you described it, the generated code, test runs, deployments, and all iterations as you refine the product.

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Does one job = one app?">
    Yes. Each job corresponds to exactly one application. If you want to build a weather dashboard and a recipe tracker, those are two separate jobs.
    
    Everything tied to a single app — code, dependencies, deployment config, chat context — lives within that job's workspace.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I manage multiple jobs?">
    Your workspace lists all your jobs in the sidebar. Click any job name to switch to it and load its chat, code, and deployment history.
    
    You can rename, archive, or delete jobs from the job settings menu (accessed via the three-dot icon next to the job name). Archiving a job removes it from the active list but preserves all its data.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I work on multiple jobs at the same time?">
    The workspace UI focuses on one job at a time, but you can open multiple browser tabs or windows — each pointing to a different job — and work in parallel.
    
    Builds, tests, and deployments run independently per job, so starting a build in one job does not block another.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What happens when I fork a job?">
    Forking creates a new job that starts with a copy of the current job's code and state. This is useful when you want to explore a different direction or experiment without affecting the original.
    
    The forked job is fully independent: changes in one do not affect the other. For more detail, see [Forking](/forking).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Do jobs cost credits individually?">
    Yes. Each job consumes credits based on its own build, test, and deployment activity. Building and iterating on multiple jobs in parallel will use credits from your account balance accordingly.
    
    For pricing details, see [How credits work](/how-credits-work).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Projects

<Info>
**Projects** let you group related jobs together for easier organisation. A project is simply a folder that contains multiple jobs — think of it as a way to keep all the apps for a client, a product suite, or a learning experiment in one place.
</Info>

To create a project, use the "New Project" option in the workspace sidebar. You can then move existing jobs into it or create new jobs directly inside the project.

Switching between projects updates the sidebar to show only the jobs within that project. You can always return to the "All Jobs" view to see everything across all projects.

Projects are purely organisational — they do not share code, dependencies, or configuration between jobs. Each job inside a project remains independent.
description: 1. What a Job is: a single build/app/project in Emergent - the term you'll see across the platform.
